Amazon attributed the 2024 increase in AWS operating income mainly to higher sales, lower payroll and related expenses, and lower depreciation and amortization after its server useful-life change. It said spending on technology infrastructure partly offset these gains. AWS sales rose 19%. Consolidated operating income rose about 86.1%, shown as context only because it is not the AWS segment change.
Amazon said the increase in AWS operating income in 2024 was primarily due to increased sales, decreased payroll and related expenses, and a reduction in depreciation and amortization expense from its change in the estimated useful lives of its servers. It said these were partially offset by spending on technology infrastructure, primarily driven by additional investments to support AWS business growth.
On the sales driver, Amazon said AWS sales increased 19% in 2024. It said the growth primarily reflects increased customer usage, partially offset by pricing changes primarily driven by long-term customer contracts.
Amazon said the server and networking equipment useful life changes primarily impact the AWS segment. It said the changes are due to an increased pace of technology development, particularly in the area of artificial intelligence and machine learning. It also said accelerated depreciation will continue into 2025 and decrease operating income by approximately $0.6 billion in 2025.
Amazon said the majority of infrastructure costs recorded in Technology and infrastructure are allocated to the AWS segment based on usage. This is why infrastructure spending to support AWS growth weighs on AWS segment profit.
As context only, Amazon's consolidated operating income grew about 86.1% in FY2024 versus FY2023 (from $36.85 billion to $68.59 billion). This is not the AWS segment change.
